messages:
maya: Heads-up — I kicked off an experiment for P95-driven batching. Idea: per-route / per-tier dynamic token budgets that scale to keep p95 <= 250ms. Posting the config and a couple quick profiling notes here.

liam: Nice, what control loop cadence are you using?

maya: 30s windows with EWMA smoothing (alpha=0.25). Simple rule: if p95 > target reduce token_budget by 15% (floor 8 tokens), if p95 < target increase by 10% until route max. Also backoff on oscillation for 3 cycles.

eva: Can you paste the rollout snippet so eng-sre can review?

maya: Sure — config we pushed to the canary (prod-2):

```
{
  "route": "route:chat-generation",
  "tier": "standard",
  "p95_target_ms": 250,
  "control_window_s": 30,
  "smoothing": {"type": "ewma", "alpha": 0.25},
  "adjustments": {"down_pct": 0.15, "up_pct": 0.10, "min_tokens": 8, "max_tokens": 256},
  "cache_aware": {"cold_kv_bonus_pct": 30, "bonus_requests": 10}
}
```

ash: How are you handling KV cache warm-up? If budgets drop too fast cold-cache traffic could spike p95.

maya: Added a cache-aware multiplier — requests tagged as cold-kv (based on kv_miss_ratio heuristic) get +30% token allowance for first 10 requests per key. We also track per-key heat to avoid gaming.

liam: Any changes to kernel selection/packing logic? Small microbatches usually pick different kernels — could add overhead.

maya: Good call. Profiling shows kernel selection overhead goes up ~3-5ms when microbatch size < 4 because we fall back to the single-threaded GEMM path. But overall tail improves for short sequencessince queues drain faster. Snapshot from profiler:

```
[2026-03-16T15:12:03Z] route=chat-gen tier=standard microbatch=2 seq_p95=230ms kernel_choice=scalar_gemm sel_cost=4.3ms
[2026-03-16T15:12:03Z] route=chat-gen tier=standard microbatch=8 seq_p95=260ms kernel_choice=fused_gemm sel_cost=1.0ms
```

maya: Net effect for our workload (median tokens ~12) was p95 down ~10-12% on canary while GPU utilization increased ~6%.

perf-bot: perf-check: route=chat-gen@prod-2 before p95=274ms after initial policy p95=241ms (1h canary). retry_rate +0.4%, infra-errors unchanged.

ryan: Can we gate by route tier? e.g. premium routes get higher max_tokens and slower shrink rate. Also run a 1h canary then promote.

maya: Yep — tier overrides are part of the schema. Canary started at 1784507600 on prod-2; monitoring dashboards hooked (per-route p95, retry rate, kv_miss_ratio).

eva: :thumbsup: Please watch for increased retry_rate or sudden spikes in latency for longer-context requests. If retry_rate > 1% rollback.

maya: Will do. Also adding a queue-length safeguard: if queue_length > 1200 we temporarily halt growth and bias towards latency (force shrink).

ash: One more: instrument the kernel selection hotpath to emit sel_cost histogram to tracing so we can correlate with p95.

maya: Added — next push includes `runtime.kernel.sel_cost_ms` metric and a small trace span.

liam: Thanks. If the sel_cost correlation looks bad we should consider a hybrid policy: keep slightly larger microbatches for routes with high sel_cost variance.

maya: Agreed. Will post updated perf graphs in ~30m.

perf-bot: alert: canary p95 crossing thresholds? no — stable. next check in 10m.
